quest.title: An Odd Textual Mystery
quest.description: Collei tells you that Sumeru's been quite lively lately. As such, you and Paimon resolve to see what's going on...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Didn't Collei say Sumeru City has been pretty lively lately? Aren't you even a little curious?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What—Hey! C'mon, don't be so cold, show Paimon your passion, your passion! You can just think of it as accompanying Paimon to the party, okay...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, okay, Paimon. I'll be your chaperone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's go see what's going on! Um... For our first stop, maybe start with the Akademiya? That's where all the info is, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right!? Paimon agrees!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, that's Faruzan over there! Do you think we should ask...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: ...Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ugh! Even just glancing at the borrowing records gives me flashbacks to how awful that book was... How irritating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Faruzan! What are you doing talking to yourself over here?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I am Madam Faruzan, after all. It's not out of place for me to mull things over out loud, wouldn't you say? But in this case...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: *sigh* Never mind, forget about it. Why'd the two of you suddenly decide to drop by?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, er, about that... we heard something about a party, and didn't want to miss out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei told us that Sumeru's the place to be now! Apparently tons of interesting things are happening, so we thought we'd ask around. Any idea what she was talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Interesting things... What might Collei find interesting? Tighnari's tail getting so fluffed up like a ball of tumbleweed? Or Cyno climbing a tree and getting his hood caught on a branch?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, we really missed all that...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seriously? And nobody thought to tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, she said there was something big everyone's been talking about. Can you think of anything... slightly more significant?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: More significant...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Ah!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is something the matter, Madam?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Umm, well, err... Ahh! Now that you mention it, it must be what I think it is!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Recently, rumors have been going around about "a certain book."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek, that's a classic horror story opening! It's not some kind of forbidden tome or anything like that, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Forbidden tome? Ha! As far as I'm concerned, it might as well be. Tell me, have you ever read one of those really, really, really badly-written detective novels?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

choices.text: Uh... I don't think I have...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has, Paimon has!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Tell me exactly how bad it was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oohhh, leave this to Paimon! For example, the type where you start off thinking it's a locked room murder mystery, but it actually turns out that the whole building was just moved...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: That's right! Or it's supposed to be based on pure reasoning and logical deduction, but at the end, it turns out that the culprit has some kind of superpower...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Or it starts out suuuper serious, but in the second half, it just reveals that everyone lost their memories out of the blue!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Or it's set in a mountain village in the middle of a snowstorm, and the police officer who's been portrayed as a serious figure throughout the whole story suddenly turns out to be the murderer, without even the slightest hint of foreshadowing!

choices.text: You're both being way too specific...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Ahem... My apologies, I let myself get a bit carried away there for a moment. Anyway, to cut a long story short, I did borrow a book like that a few days past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you borrowed a badly written book... But that happens to the best of us!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: No, that's the problem. Blizzard-swept mountain villages, superpowers, police officers who turn out to be criminals... This book had it all, and more! Reading it was tantamount to torture.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: And despite how complicated it was, it wasn't engaging in the slightest!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: But there have been all sorts of rumors circulating about this book. Because of the strange marks drawn over all the pages, people are saying that it must be concealing secrets.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you think there's treasure involved?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I'm not sure, but there must be many who believe so. Not only have more and more people been borrowing it, but they've all been specifically asking for "the marked-up copy."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you borrowed it too?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Yes, I have! As you well know, I am a scholar, so it's only natural to have a bit of curiosity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, just what secrets does the book at the center of the rumors actually hold?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I read through carefully from start to finish. Most of the marks are circles, but the beginning and end points of each stroke differ, as does the color of the ink used...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Most importantly, all the names of people in the book have been circled. Not only that, many of them are adapted from famous figures in Sumeru's history.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Some speculate that these marks must have been left by different scholars over the eras, each researching the book's secrets, each searching for a name they believed in.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Others believe that they are a kind of notation made by different people belonging to the same organization, and that the names circled are their code names.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Still others think that it is some kind of encryption cipher, but even after finishing it, I came no closer to uncovering the mystery. Not only was reading it a complete waste of my time, but sheer absurdity of the shoddy excuse for a plot several times over...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I was so angry that I returned the book immediately. And when I came to the House of Daena today, I found lots of people skulking around — I suppose they're all still looking for that... thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder you zoned out like that. Paimon's guessing you won't be borrowing any more detective novels anytime soon...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: #Indeed... *sigh* ...Paimon, {NICKNAME}, surely the two of you must understand how I feel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's the book called? We'll borrow it and take a look ourselves.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: It's called "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds more like the title of a light novel!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: *sigh* Tell me about it. Anyway, read it at your own risk. It truly is unbearably boring...

choices.text: You sure it's a detective novel?
Don't worry, Madam. I feel your frustration.
You'll offend half the crime novelists in Teyvat if you keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's so many books with long titles here, let Paimon have a look... "Working Hard and Vacationing Harder," what the heck?

choices.text: "An Atlas of Rare Rainforest-Dwelling Species, Professional Edition"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Secrets of the Elemental Sciences"... The book jacket even says, "Expert approved! The former Sage Cyrus praises this as an excellent entry-level book"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this one, "A Compilation and Summary of Common Basic Grammar Rules for Rare Languages of Ancient Desert Peoples"... Urk! Now Paimon's dizzy, it's just... so... so many... words...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: C'mon, Paimon! You can learn twenty different...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Is that Layla over there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's just ask her! She may know something.

choices.text: "The Art of the Construction of Coffee Machines"... Who exactly reads these?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's been so long... *yawn* I'm still a bit tired...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't sleep well last night?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Mmm, I was reading a novel, so I stayed up late.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It wasn't that detective novel that everyone's been talking about, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The one with the super long name...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, no, if you're talking about "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a..." ... Umm, follows a...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Blizzard.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, right, yes. No, it wasn't that one. Madam Faruzan said it was really dull, so I didn't borrow it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're not that interested in the book's secrets?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I haven't even been able to keep up with my own work, even though I'm up late all the time these days...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: But way more people have been interested in the book than I ever imagined, seven or eight in a single morning... I feel like a living signboard sitting here like this.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Kaveh asked me the same question, so he must be looking for it too? He was even hiding behind a ladder before, looking for something... He looked really embarrassed...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Searching for something, hiding behind a ladder... He must be after Mora! That's gotta be it, so he can hurry up and pay off his debt to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no no! Let's just pretend Paimon didn't say anything! Layla, you're really sleepy, right? You must be dreaming this conversation, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I didn't really get it anyway, but if you say so, it's a dream...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thank you, we'll keep on looking!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Okay, see you next time! ...*snore* ... *snore*...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's not often Layla falls asleep so quickly. Good for her...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks we should go ask Kaveh now. If he's searching for the book, he must know something.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But where is he now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Good question... But we can try hanging around where he might show up! There's a good chance he's there right now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D'you ever think we seem like a pair of thieves? Hiding here to ambush Kaveh, it almost feels like we're here to extort him or something...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not sure why that is though, we just want to ask him a couple of questions, that's all...

choices.text: Don't make it sound like we're the baddies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? That sounds like footsteps! Quick, let's take a look!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop right there, Ka...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Alhaitham? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Good question. Surprising indeed — I was under the impression that you knew I lived here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Good morning.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Good morning. What can I do for you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, we... Umm... Nothing, never mind!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Oh? Goodbye then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He just left... Does he have work to do or something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Footsteps, again? They're heading towards the door.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Stop right there, Kaveh!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Waaah! What in the... What are you two doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good question. Surprising indeed — Paimon was under the impression that you'd know the only reason we'd be here was if we were looking for you!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Paimon, you don't sound like yourself.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looking for a certain book, by any chance?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Wait, what!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Here's the deal...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Paimon pull Kaveh to one side and, in hushed tones, tell him about the rumors that Faruzan was talking about. You also mention that an eye-witness saw him searching for something in the House of Daena...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: ...How is it you guys know everything? Gah, and there I was, thinking I'd been super discreet the whole time. No one should even have noticed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, get real! You really think that no one knows you live here?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Hey, that's not fair! Of course nobody knows, except for Cyno, Tighnari, Collei, and the two of you... right?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Friends are friends, so if they know... well, they know! But what if a stranger overheard us? It would be a disaster! It might even impact my career...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Anyway, about that book...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You believe it contains intel about hidden treasure, doncha? Looking to get rich quick, are we?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Uh... Umm... Yeah... Are you offering to help find it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shucks, why didn't you say so earlier! So there really is treasure! How about this — we help you find it, then split the loot 50-50. It's a deal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, after all we've been through, it's finally our turn to get rich! No need to keep yapping — hidden treasure, the Paimon-probe's homin' in on ya!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Huh? Hey, Paimon!

choices.text: When have you ever been bothered by your conscience?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that... Dehya?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon? Must be my lucky day, running into you like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya, you mercenaries are pretty tuned into the grapevine. Have you ever heard of a book called "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard"?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait, you guys are looking for it too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By "too", you don't mean... you're looking for it, too!? Darn, it does... so, does that mean we're finally gonna have to square off against Dehya?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Wait a minute, would you mind telling me exactly why you're looking for it?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once more, you go over the rumors that Faruzan told you...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If it really does turn out to be something important, I'll be sure to let you know if I hear anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, r—really!? From your reaction before, Paimon thought you were after it too.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry. A client had asked me to get her the book, but her attitude seemed off somehow, so I didn't take the commission.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: She's a smart cookie, though, and it was like she was hiding something, so I thought she must have had an ulterior motive. Besides, I have other things to look into right now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Compared to some commission, it's more important that you uncover the truth behind that book. Anyway, no time to lose — I've gotta get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then, good luck! And don't forget to tell us if you hear anything!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I wonder who Dehya's client could be?)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey—!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *panting* Ha... *panting*... How are you so fast?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flying's faster than running?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Alright, listen to me... *huff*... It's, it's like this...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Paimon... don't get your hopes up. That book... It isn't some kind of treasure map. It's just an unbelievably unremarkable, surpassingly ordinary detective novel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... Didn't you just say there was treasure? If most people backtracked like that, Paimon'd just think they'd changed their mind and wanted to keep all the Mora for themselves... but that's not something you'd do!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: No, that's... I, uh... *sigh* I'm sorry, I just couldn't bring myself to tell you earlier, so I played along with what you were saying.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Here's what happened... I borrowed the book a month ago. When I opened it to the first page, I discovered one of the names was printed incorrectly.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: That night, I'd been drinking — just a little — and I was starting to feel drowsy, so I picked up a pen, and circled the name.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: As I'm sure you know, the House of Daena allows borrowers to annotate the books they take out. I'm in the habit of doing that too, so at the time, I didn't give it a second thought.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: But after I was a dozen or so pages in, I realized that the names of all the characters in the book had intentionally been written slightly wrong.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Maybe it would be more accurate to say that the novel itself was... quite strange. All the characters' names were based on real historical figures, but rather than using their original names, they had been tweaked ever so slightly...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Most people would assume that the author had made a mistake or that there'd been a printing error when they saw spelling mistakes like that.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: I didn't find the content particularly appealing, so I returned it before I finished reading it.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: But later on, I heard that the book had suddenly become the talk of the town, and that there were rumors about mysterious treasure or something...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And you thought it had something to do with you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It certainly does sound like it.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Yeah... And I also heard that now, all the names in the book have been circled, not just one.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: I just haven't been able to figure out what in Teyvat must have happened after I returned it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you tell anyone else that you borrowed it?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Let me think... Uhh, Tighnari?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Last time we met, I also told him all about how poorly parts of the book were written. He said I'd made it sound pretty funny — so much so, in fact, that he suddenly wanted to take a look himself.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You made it sound like it was "so bad it's good"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, let's go find Tighnari!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: That's fine with me, but I still have some work to finish up, and it's pretty urgent. How about I head back first and we can meet up again later once I'm done?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem, hope your work goes well!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Me too, thanks! See you later then.

choices.text: Having been through so much, I run fast...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there, over there! Hey, Tigh—na—riiii—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #I heard you, I heard you! How's it going, {NICKNAME} and Paimon? You guys sure look excited.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Tighnari about how you're looking for the novel "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you do so, you reflect once more on how absurdly long the title is, and how even just saying it aloud makes you feel tired...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there's Dehya! Let's tell her what the real story is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Candace is there too.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...So, I need to reflect a little on what I did.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: To meet you here today is surely due to the guidance of the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greetings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace, is this a personal trip?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Today's trip to the city is to buy provisions for the people of Aaru Village, as well as help Miss Setaria deliver a message to the sages of the Akademiya while I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: On the way, I happened to see Dehya sitting in the cafe looking down, so I came over to chat with her.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's nothing serious. It's just that I suddenly remembered a few details about that book after talking with you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Before that client had even contacted me, I'd heard rumors of an exciting novel full of undiscovered secrets. Out of curiosity, I asked Cyno to take it out for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: As a desert-dweller, and a mercenary to boot, the idea of solving a mysterious treasure map is pretty exciting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, Paimon totally gets that.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: We inherited our custom of searching for the gold and wisdom in the sands from the gods themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But that book turned out to be dry as dust. A bunch of names had been circled, but I still couldn't figure out what the puzzle was supposed to be despite reading the whole thing through carefully from start to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: In the end, I started to think it was some kind of ritual, or game, or something, so I picked up a pen and drew a circle of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But later on, Miss Dunyarzad asked her parents to find a way to borrow it for her. She said the mysterious markings fascinated her, even though she couldn't get into the book itself.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If they were just regular annotations, it wouldn't be anything out of the ordinary, but these strange circles... You can't help but want to try and figure out what they might mean.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's true. So, Dehya, what you're reflecting on is having accidentally interfered with other people's reading experiences, is that correct?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hold on a second! Why did you tell Candace?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: She's a warrior, you know. Sometimes she has to interrogate criminals and other things like that too. Everyone recognizes that her job is sacred, so when we need to think over what we've gone wrong, we'll talk to her about it.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #Please, don't be too surprised, my dear {NICKNAME}. To me, listening to other people's mistakes is just another way of protecting them.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: By speaking of your own mistakes and hearing sincere advice in return, improvement will come, over time. That's the way we do things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... all she did was draw a circle, and it's not like she was deliberately trying to mess with anyone... Beside, everyone agrees that the book itself is just bad. Don't worry about it, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's true. I was just telling Candace how bizarre it is...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: But be that as it may, it doesn't change the fact that it just ain't right to mess with someone else's enjoyment of a book. That's the bottom line.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Anyway, Dehya, please have faith that the gods will forgive your transgression.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Besides, you told me about a part of the story where one of the suspects in the case ended up crawling out of the village on his hands and knees, and he was named... "Al-Ahmal."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's right. The detective in the book argued that he must have leapt across the broken bridge like a frog. Of course, you find out later on his conjecture was totally off base.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Because it turns out that "Al-Ahmal" has a superpower, so he could float right across the broken bridge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What the heck is the book even about? It sounds completely ludicrous.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: "Al-Ahmal"... It's simply too reminiscent of the good name of King Deshret, don't you think? Though considering how transgressive this book sounds, I don't think it's worth overthinking it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You're right. *sigh* Y'know, I can't help but wonder what our friends at the Temple of Silence would say if they somehow got their hands on this book.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm sure those sages would be able to unpack interesting ideas from the text we ordinary people could scarce dream of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's normal for there to be bridges outside blizzard-swept mountain villages, and normal for them to get broken, but for a person to cross one by floating through the air... Why resort to such a lame plot device?

choices.text: Is it really a serious detective novel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's starting to get where Faruzan was coming from. If you'd gotten all excited about reading a detective novel, but ended up reading tripe like that instead... Ugh, better not to even think about it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, where's the book now?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Not sure. I returned it after I was done reading it, and back then, there weren't as many markings inside as the rumors say there are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then Detective Paimon is still on this case!

choices.text: Sounds more like something out of a comic strip...

talks.objective: Go to the House of Daena

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello! Has "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard" been returned yet?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: There are two copies of this book — one's been marked up, the other hasn't. I'm guessing you're looking for the one with the marks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! You saw right through us...

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Many others have asked for it too. I apologize though, it seems it hasn't been returned yet. Please come back again later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't you at least tell us who borrowed it?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Well... As long as it isn't overdue, we'll wait patiently for it to be returned.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Disclosing borrowers' identities without proper reason for doing so would be a violation of professional ethics, so you'll have to forgive me for keeping that information confidential.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got a point. It would be terrible if someone looking to steal a book started harassing whoever had borrowed it...
Hey, you two look as confused as a couple of Aranara who've just run into each other headfirst. Are you looking for something? I can help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's Nahida's voice!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hi there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nahida! Have you heard of a book called "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard"?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Such a long name... But, yes, I know the one you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I heard that everyone was looking for it, and it sounded fascinating, so I found a brand-new copy to read myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By "brand-new," do you mean it wasn't the copy with all the markings on it?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. I was more interested in the content of the book itself than all those rumors about hidden treasure, so an unmarked copy was all I needed.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, it's funny — there's more than one copy of this book, but everyone's looking for the one where all the names have been circled. Are they all afraid of spoilers, or do they actually crave them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, then do you know who has the copy with the markings right now?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I just so happen to have seen it in the hands of one of your friends. If you're looking for the copy that's sparked all the rumors, you should look around near the Palace of Alcazarzaray.

talks.objective: Go to the Palace of Alcazarzaray

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that... Huh? Dori, Cyno... and Sethos?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Aaaaah! Darn you, General Mahamatra, entrapment isn't gonna work! You can't do that!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Hey, what do you mean by "entrapment"?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You were the one who said you had the book. I said I wanted to read it, then you agreed to meet me here. Cyno showing up too was just a coincidence, pure coincidence!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You, you... Don't play games with me, I know who you are! You're that new kid Sethos, right? I know you're a friend of Cyno's.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Huh, so you do know who I am.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I saw how Cyno was chasing you around, trying to get you to play cards, and how you found an excuse to run off after a couple of rounds right after. That left quite an impression.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You didn't have to mention that...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No, I think Dori's right about that. You always look for a way out when it comes to playing Invokation — it's becoming quite a problem.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, you've been standing there for quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Oh! I—If it isn't... if it isn't my dear {NICKNAME} and Paimon! What brings the two of you to the Palace of Alcazarzaray?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Might it be that you have come to do business with me, the Lord Sangemah Bay? Hahaha, of course, of course! Please, give me a moment to conclude our business here, then I'll be with you straight away.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Anyway, General Mahamatra, as I am sure you are well aware, the means by which I had someone borrow this book from the House of Daena were both completely legal and perfectly reasonable.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Seeing as it isn't yet time to return it, you have no right to forcibly seize a book I borrowed!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That would only be the case had you not engaged in any irregular activities.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yet just now, a buyer — Sethos — came to the Palace of Alcazarzaray on the basis of a mysterious message to meet a seller, hoping in vain to purchase a detective novel.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "buyer"? He's one of your people! You sent him here to deliberately try to buy it and entrap me!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That is not something I can acknowledge. What I can tell you is that I've had my eyes on this book for some time. Remember, it is forbidden to transfer or sell books from the House of Daena without explicit approval from the relevant authorities.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmph! I'm not selling anything, just to be clear. I'm just making the most of an opportunity. If someone pays me a little something on the side, I lend them this mysterious little novel to "browse" for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: If you don't believe me, just ask any of my custom... Er, I mean, curious readers! Yes, that's right, you're readers. Anyway, I was just showing him the book.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Is that so? And here I was thinking you were really going to go through with an illegal transaction like this, Sethos.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, what? You two really aren't together?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I was just really curious about this book. I finally managed to track it down, but Cyno... It's true that Dori never actually said she wanted to "sell" the book.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Tsk. So she isn't the mastermind who started all this?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: The mastermind...? Hehehe, so by your own account, it looks like you might've jumped the gun a bit, General Mahamatra. I'm not handing the book over.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmph. You may think you've played an ace, Dori. But when you opened the book just now, I saw the truth revealed before me... the book's return date is today!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ugh...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno, you've sure got sharp eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right, I do have good vision. You have less than half an hour before the book is overdue. Give it to me, and I will return it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmph... How could I... Just hand it over to you like that... This is a mysterious, super awesome mega-amazing paragon of illogical detective novels that is practically a treasure! I'm gonna make a fortune off of it!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Should you really be admitting that out loud...?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I didn't say I was going to sell it! It's not like I was being serious.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Then how about this? Dori, Cyno, why don't you two play a little game, with the book as the stakes?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's one way of solving it. How about it, Dori? Do you dare accept the challenge? If you win, I'll turn a blind eye to the book for the time being. And if you lose, you have to hand it over.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh? Sounds interesting. Very well, I'm in. What's the contest?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Are both of you confident in your powers of mental recall?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: My memory's not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: And you have both read the contents of this book, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Huh? Cyno, you've actually read it? Oho! Well, needless to say, so have I.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll just open up the book and flip through a few pages, and you tell me how many names have been circled. Best out of three wins. Sound good?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ehhhh!? That's nuts!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What, chickening out?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: No, it's game on. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Good. In that case, the first page.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Six!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Six.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Both correct! Next, the second page.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmm... I think it was four?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'd say four.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh! Both of you are right again! Two draws, so it all hangs on the next question. Listen up!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: —Page 61.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ehh? What!? That... I... uh... I... don't quite remember... um, seven?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I know. The answer is... five!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Absolutely correct! The answer is five.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Urk! Cyno, i—is your memory really that good? I'm not buying it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did you do that?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's not actually because I have a good memory, but because the circling of the names left a deep impression on me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: After I borrowed it, I noticed the names on the first few pages had been selectively circled by different people.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Each person's penmanship was different, and moreover, I recognized three of the circles as having been drawn by Tighnari. Few others use the same color of ink as he does, so it was instantly recognizable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You even know that?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes, I learned of that habit of his long ago. At that time, I had just been promoted General Mahamatra, and would go to a secret base when I wanted to get through all the trivial tasks in my in-tray at once with minimal disturbances.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I would often find Tighnari hidden away on a tree there, doing his homework. Noticing the writing implements he favored wasn't exactly detective work. In all these years, he's never once changed the ink he uses.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Back to that book. Anyone who's read it knows that the first name circled is the real murderer. Perhaps Tighnari did not want the plot to be spoiled for anyone else, so he circled other names.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Annotating or marking a book is not in itself a violation of book-borrowing regulations. But why are all the other marks there? Is there some conspiracy behind them? What do they have to do with Tighnari?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I want to get to the bottom of this, even it's just for the sake of my friend. And to uncover the secret, you must become a part of the conspiracy. So, I circled all the other names that were left in the book!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Wha—!? To think you'd do such a thing... So there's no treasure at all, it was just you guys all along!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right. Should you wish to hide a grain of sand, bury it in the desert. And in that grain of sand, I can catch a glimpse of the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And so you were drawn to it, making your plans, yet in a twist of fate, were discovered by me. No matter how vast this world is, you cannot run from the long arm of the law.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Wow, you're making a meal out of this, aren't you? You really, really... have way too much time on your hands. Okay, I give up, you win.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *cough* Ahem! That's enough for today. It is time for Lord Sangemah Bay to return to her room for some repose. Farewell, all!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So, do you intend to take this book back to the Temple of Silence?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I'd heard there was treasure hidden inside, and thought it might have something to do with the Temple. I never thought that was the real story behind it.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: But when you agreed to compete, I had already surmised you were familiar with this book. That's why I chose that particular format.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Brilliant move, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's with that look?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're just thinking... There have been more twists and turns in the story behind the book than in the actual story itself...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, as long as you got it back! I'll leave uncovering the rest of the secrets to you, and take my leave for now. See you later, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can I borrow the book?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After Cyno hands you the book, you and Paimon quickly thumb through it. Though you weren't reading very carefully, you can tell that something's not quite right...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The plot is wildly imaginative. And just as everyone says, though most of the names in the book seem familiar, on closer inspection, you realize that they aren't actually the names of the historical figures you thought they were at first.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Not only that, but every name has been circled. Thinking back on the course of events, you fall silent... And then, you explain the full story.

talks.objective: Return to the House of Daena

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we're finally back. Now, let's return this book...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You really found the book? Amazing! I've been waiting here for it to be returned, so I could see it as soon as possible!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount the entire tale to Kaveh's eager ears...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah!? Seriously? How is that even possible? I... I... I circled the actual murderer!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's pretty surprised by this whole thing too...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Let's just take care of the book problem first.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hello, this book, it, um... It's probably all my fault for using permanent ink to mark a page, since that caused a whole mess of other things to happen...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Now it's all marked up like this, and there's even a risk of those marks spoiling the story, so I'd like to buy it. The whole issue should be avoidable if the Akademiya uses the money to buy a new copy.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Would you please consider my proposal?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Kaveh, your idea has merit, and it is indeed a good way to resolve this situation. I'll confirm the book's price now, and then you can pay over there.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's great. Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Shortly afterwards, Kaveh accompanies the Akademiya staff to register the purchase of the book and pays the full amount.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The staff member carefully wraps up the thoroughly marked-up old book and gives it to him.

talks.objective: Catch up to Kaveh as he leaves

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah, Alhaitham! You're here! I was looking everywhere for you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Haha, guess what I've got in this little bag here?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If I had to guess— A young man's tears of regret.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And what would you know! It's "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You actually bothered to memorize a ridiculous and boring name like that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's just because when I was filling out the paperwork to buy it back at the Akademiya's office, I had to write it out over and over.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Then it looks like this book has a new owner.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Only because I subconsciously marked up the book with ink!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Did you know that Tighnari, Dehya, and Cyno all circled names in the book? And it all started because the name I circled was the real killer.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Ah. To be perfectly honest, the moment I first saw the murderer's name circled, I knew this would happen.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait a second, how come you've read the book too?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I had the pleasure of reading it in the House of Daena. The logic is a mess, it's just poorly written.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And you left the book out in the study.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So you knew I circled the killer? Then... then did you circle any names in the book?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...So you did?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The second one is mine.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Why!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The best way to avoid spoilers is to add a red herring.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Then why just one? Tighnari circled three!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I already significantly reduced the probability of the murderer's identity being spoiled for the next reader, that's more than enough. No need to worry about things that are beyond saving.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And just why isn't it necessary?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Using permanent ink to circle a name on the first page. That's obviously beyond saving.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What kind of logic is that? I bet you just drew your circle for fun!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If I must say so, then it's because the circling of the names is far more interesting than the book itself.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* Fair point.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: In the end, I only have myself to blame for using up all my pencils... I need to go buy some more.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Congratulations. This one-of-a-kind, out-of-print book, personally penned by the hands of so many, is now yours.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Do you think I look happy about it!? *sigh* I don't even want it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahaha... If it was Paimon, she wouldn't want it either!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's a no from me too...)

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm? You want to know what kind of books I like?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: The spectrum is just so broad, I don't know where to start...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Zzz... Zzz...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Who could've predicted this?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It is precisely because it is unpredictable that you shouldn't blame yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It seems there's a story behind that story...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go see if there's any other clues. We'll definitely be able to find out more by asking around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's feeling lost... Maybe we should head back to the House of Daena?
